newsitem.title: USA: U.S. criticizes Japan's aviation bargaining tactic.
newsitem.headline: U.S. criticizes Japan's aviation bargaining tactic.

text.p: A senior White House official Thursday criticised Japan for linking the safety of a U.S. airline to negotiations with the United States over a new, liberal aviation agreement.

"Casting aspersions about safety practices just has no place in international air services negotiations," Daniel Tarullo, assistant to President Clinton for international economics, told the International Aviation Club.
"To make safety and scare tactics on safety a negotiating advantage of some sort is simply unacceptable," Tarullo said.
He referred to Japanese Ministry of Transport complaints on the safety record of Northwest Airlines Corp. and asked the Federal Aviation Administration to investigate.

A Northwest spokesman said Japan, which cited 27 Northwest "incidents" in the past 15 months, linked safety to a liberal, "open skies" regime that it said led to excess competition and reductions in maintenance.

But the FAA said the 27 events were not "incidents" as it defined them -- potential safety hazards -- but only mechanical malfunctions expected even in airlines flying at the highest levels of safety and aircraft reliability.
It said Japan's safety complaints were unfounded.
"Safety in aviation is an independent and really paramount goal for this government," Tarullo said.
The United States and Japan have been meeting over the past year to try to resolve problems in their current air pact and to set the stage for talks on a more liberal accord.
